gen_risks.description: Fragmented and obsolete PFM information systems may cause implementation delays and increased costs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a detailed system‑integration roadmap, adopt common data standards, and pilot modules before full rollout.
gen_risks.evidence: Core PFM information systems suffer from fragmentation, obsolescence, and weak institutional support.

gen_risks.description: Cyber‑attacks on government portals could disrupt new PFM platforms and data integrity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement ISMS, establish a Security Operations Center, conduct regular penetration testing and staff cyber‑hygiene training.
gen_risks.evidence: Superintendency of Tax Administration faced >8,000 cyber‑attacks in 2021; Guatecompras and SICOIN stopped working due to a cyber‑attack in 2023.

gen_risks.description: Absence of an ISMS/BCMS would leave systems vulnerable to disruptions and data loss.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finalize ISMS/BCMS early, obtain ISO‑27001/22301 certification, and run tabletop continuity exercises.
gen_risks.evidence: Subcomponent 2.5 will develop an Information Security Management System (ISMS) and Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) to ensure response to disruptive incidents.

gen_risks.description: Decline in remittance inflows could reduce VAT collections, shrinking fiscal space for the project.
gen_risks.mitigation: Build fiscal buffers, monitor remittance trends quarterly, diversify revenue sources, and adjust budget forecasts accordingly.
gen_risks.evidence: Remittances ≈19.4% GDP; any decline could reduce VAT collections, which generate 47.8% of net income.

gen_risks.description: IFMIS modernization may experience cost overruns, threatening the budget.
gen_risks.mitigation: Institute independent cost monitoring, set a contingency reserve (10% of component budget), and enforce strict procurement controls.
gen_risks.evidence: IFMIS projects tend to be costly and lengthy and should be realistically appraised.

gen_risks.description: Delay in establishing the PIU would block Category 1 withdrawals and disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign senior MINFIN officials to PIU creation, track milestone completion weekly, and report to the Bank.
gen_risks.evidence: No withdrawal shall be made under Category 1 until the Borrower has established the PIU, satisfactory to the Bank.

gen_risks.description: Missing June 2025 deadlines for IPSAS adoption, enterprise architecture, and security policies could delay outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use a milestone‑tracking tool, allocate dedicated staff for each deliverable, and conduct monthly progress reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: IPSAS adopted (Jun 2025); Information security and business continuity policy defined and adopted (Jun 2025).

gen_risks.description: Insufficient political commitment or turnover of reform champions could stall reforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure a formal high‑level commitment letter, embed reform targets in ministerial performance contracts, and create incentive mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: A common reason for failure … lack of adequate preparation and institutional stability; need for sustained commitment from senior leadership.

gen_risks.description: Weak coordination among MINFIN, SEGEPLAN and other agencies may impede implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Draft a clear governance charter, schedule regular joint meetings, and appoint a coordination lead with authority to resolve conflicts.
gen_risks.evidence: Digital Transformation Committee and Inter‑institutional Committee will serve as governance bodies to ensure inclusive participation and strategic coordination.

gen_risks.description: Failure to establish grievance mechanism within 60 days breaches legal covenant.
gen_risks.mitigation: Designate a grievance‑mechanism officer, set internal deadline of 45 days, and report status to the Bank.
gen_risks.evidence: Borrower shall establish the Project grievance mechanism no later than sixty (60) days after the Effective Date.

gen_risks.description: Failure to contract an external audit firm within 6 months breaches legal covenant.
gen_risks.mitigation: Issue RFP within 30 days, pre‑qualify firms, and fast‑track contract signing.
gen_risks.evidence: Borrower shall contract an external, independent private audit firm … no later than six (6) months as of the Effective Date.

gen_risks.description: Extreme weather events could damage ICT infrastructure, affecting system uptime.
gen_risks.mitigation: Harden data‑centers, locate backup sites in low‑risk zones, and include climate‑resilient design in ICT procurement.
gen_risks.evidence: Heat waves, hurricanes, storms could affect capacity of systems that provide administrative services under such circumstances.

gen_risks.description: Limited data‑analytics capacity hampers effective use of new PFM platforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Launch structured training programmes, recruit data analysts, and create a career path for analytics staff.
gen_risks.evidence: Weak analytical capacity, lack of structured career paths for data professionals, insufficient training.

gen_risks.description: Withdrawal of IMF/IDB technical assistance would reduce reform support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formalise MOUs with IMF and IDB, include joint work‑plans, and maintain regular liaison meetings.
gen_risks.evidence: Strong synergy with IMF (IPSAS strategy) and IDB (data quality) – parallel initiatives support the project.

gen_risks.description: Complex World Bank procurement rules could cause delays in acquiring goods and services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct early procurement readiness assessment, train staff on World Bank regulations, and use pre‑approved templates.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement will be carried out following World Bank procedure … detailed procedures in Annex 1.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risks are considered Substantial. PFM reforms typically require a whole-of-government approach and involve complex, cross-cutting changes that are often difficult to implement; these challenges are further amplified when reforms involve development or integration of sophisticated information systems. Many of the anticipated efficiency gains depend heavily on interoperability of processes and seamless integration of information systems across institutions, and the involvement of multiple stakeholders adds further complexity and increases the potential for misalignment or implementation delays.
gt_risks.mitigation: The project design includes the development and application of well-defined, evidence-based PFM conceptual and governance models, informed by a diagnostic and reform strategy developed through stakeholder consultations, providing a clear and coherent framework expected to foster shared understanding, facilitate collaboration, and reduce fragmentation.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risks are Substantial. Given the complexity of PFM reforms, the project requires strong government commitment to ensure effective implementation and safeguard long-term sustainability. Since the project's beneficiaries extend beyond MINFIN, coordination challenges may arise during implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: A PIU will be established within the Directorate of Public Treasury (DTP) for faster decision-making and improved coordination across MINFIN directorates. Component 3 will strengthen PIU operations (project management, financial management, procurement, monitoring, E&S risk management capacities); the Bank will provide training to the PIU and relevant stakeholders and facilitate change management mechanisms and a communications strategy. Coordination challenges involving multiple beneficiaries will be addressed through collaboration between MINFIN and SEGEPLAN via the Digital Transformation Commission.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risks are Substantial. This is due to DTP's limited experience with donor-funded projects and lack of recent engagement with World Bank operations; DTP has no prior experience implementing the Bank's procurement regulations, and the low value of anticipated contracts may limit interest from international firms, reducing competition. DTP has basic financial management systems in place but its unfamiliarity with the Bank's FM policies and requirements may pose risks to achieving the PDO, potentially leading to delays in activity execution.
gt_risks.mitigation: Measures include setting up a PIU with qualified personnel, offering procurement training to PIU and DTP staff, conducting market analysis to find potential providers, and preparing a simplified Project Procurement Strategy for Development (PPSD).
